text:
Encounter Summary:
- 75-year-old female with documented “type 2 diabetes for 20 years.”
- Recently “lost to follow-up.”
- Review of symptoms is negative for “increased polyuria/polydipsia, blurred vision, limb numbness, edema, intermittent claudication.”
- Exam documents “no diabetic foot, normal touch sensation.”
- HbA1c is 7.2.

Documentation Gaps:
1. Diabetes complication status not explicitly stated
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM diabetes coding depends on whether complications are present and linked to diabetes. The excerpt supports diabetes, but the note does not explicitly document whether the patient currently has type 2 diabetes with or without complications.
- Evidence quote: “type 2 diabetes for 20 years”; “Denies… blurred vision, limb numbness, edema, intermittent claudication. Exam: no diabetic foot, normal touch sensation. HbA1c 7.2.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Whether the patient’s type 2 diabetes is currently documented as without complications, or whether any diabetic complication exists and should be specified and linked.

2. Glycemic status/control terminology is not explicitly documented
- Why it matters: An HbA1c value alone does not establish a coded condition such as hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, or poor control. If the provider intends to describe glycemic status, it should be stated explicitly.
- Evidence quote: “HbA1c 7.2.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Whether there is any clinically relevant glycemic abnormality or whether diabetes is simply being followed without documented complication.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Diabetes complication specificity
- Reason query is needed: The note documents long-standing type 2 diabetes and several negative findings, but does not explicitly state complication status.
- Evidence quote: “type 2 diabetes for 20 years”; “Denies increased polyuria/polydipsia, blurred vision, limb numbness, edema, intermittent claudication. Exam: no diabetic foot, normal touch sensation.”
- Non-leading query text: “For this encounter, please clarify the current status of the patient’s type 2 diabetes mellitus based on your clinical assessment and documented findings.”
- Suggested response options:
  - Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications
  - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with complication(s) — please specify type and relationship to diabetes
  - History of diabetes only / not addressed at this encounter
  - Other
  - Clinically undetermined

2. Topic: Glycemic status terminology
- Reason query is needed: The chart includes “HbA1c 7.2” but no explicit assessment terminology regarding glycemic status.
- Evidence quote: “HbA1c 7.2.”
- Non-leading query text: “Please clarify whether there is any additional assessment regarding the patient’s glycemic status that should be documented for this encounter, if clinically applicable.”
- Suggested response options:
  - No additional glycemic abnormality documented/assessed this encounter
  - Hyperglycemia — please specify if clinically diagnosed
  - Hypoglycemia — please specify if clinically diagnosed
  - Diabetes monitored/treated without further glycemic diagnosis specified
  - Other
  - Clinically undetermined

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Diabetes type
- Presence or absence of diabetic complications
- If complications are present, the specific complication category and causal link to diabetes
- Any documented glycemic abnormality if clinically diagnosed, rather than inferred from labs alone
- Whether diabetes was actively assessed/managed during this encounter

Risk Flags:
- No explicit diabetic complication is documented; complications should not be inferred from disease duration alone.
- “HbA1c 7.2” by itself is insufficient to code hyperglycemia or uncontrolled diabetes without provider documentation.
- Negative symptom/exam findings reduce support for neuropathic, circulatory, foot, or ophthalmic complication queries beyond general clarification.
- “Recently lost to follow-up” is not itself a diagnosis codeable as a diabetic complication.

Specialist Trace:
- Medical Coding Expert: Consulted for coding specificity opportunities and compliant query targets. Accepted: support for type 2 diabetes coding framework and that E11.9 (type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications) is the most directly supported code family when no complication is documented. Rejected/limited: no patient-specific complication coding beyond what is explicitly documented.
- AMBOSS Expert: Not consulted. The excerpt does not require diagnostic criteria interpretation to identify a supported CDI clarification.
- CDI Web Search Expert: Not consulted. No current external guideline lookup was necessary for this conservative, chart-grounded CDI review.

Most supported coding impression from the excerpt alone:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus is documented.
- If the provider confirms no complications, the excerpt most closely aligns with ICD-10-CM E11.9, type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications.
- More specific complication coding is not supported by the provided documentation.
